# Northbank Learning Studio: short-workshop process

Synthetic institutional process for testing Cadence; not a real institution's policy.

This guidance applies to classroom workshops of up to 90 minutes for new staff. Use ADDIE as an iterative process. Each package must identify the learners and instructional need, explain its design, provide actual learning materials, prepare the facilitator to deliver them, and identify how the workshop will be evaluated.

The instructor plan must state duration, prerequisites, resources, observable learning objectives, and a timed sequence. Every practice activity must include learner instructions and facilitator guidance. At least one opportunity to apply feedback must appear in the sequence.

For an oral communication skill, use a performance task and a short observation checklist. A formal exam and percentage pass mark are not required for these workshops. Any proposed scoring threshold must be identified as a local design choice rather than an institutional rule.

Provide a separate learner handout and a facilitator guide. The facilitator guide must include a debrief and an adaptation for a learner who prefers to practise initially in a pair. Templates can be adapted to the topic; no additional approval checkpoint is required for draft materials.

The evaluation plan must name the evidence to collect during practice and after delivery, and explain how it will inform revision. Before actual delivery, mark implementation as prepared and outcome evaluation as planned. Do not report learner results that have not been collected.
